wy_grand_teton.blurb: The Grand is the high point of the Teton Range, at about 13,775 feet, rising directly above Jackson Hole in Grand Teton National Park. This is a serious alpine objective rather than a roadside crag. Our catalog is mostly alpine lines, with a few trad pitches and a couple of ice and mixed routes. Grades cluster around 5.8, with a solid group in the 5.10 band and a handful reaching 5.12; the easiest ways up are low fifth class with real exposure. Rock is granite. Climbing itself needs no permit, but any overnight stay does, and overnight permits for Garnet Canyon and climbing trips are picked up in person at the Jenny Lake ranger station or the main visitor center in summer. Camping is organized by permit so parties are spread out, and most climbers sleep high near the lower saddle.
wy_grand_teton.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead south of Jenny Lake, follow signs into Garnet Canyon. The maintained trail runs out at a boulder field around 4 miles in; a rougher path continues up to the lower saddle, about 5,000 feet above the car. Most parties break the day by camping in the canyon or at the saddle.
